README: Tracked JS/TS files that no coverage run measures, each with the reason it is not measured.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
assert-coverage-scope.mjs pins each package's denominator so it cannot shrink. That
catches a file being dropped from a report, but it cannot tell 'we measure 20 of 21
files and the 21st has no harness' from 'we measure 20 and lost track of one'. jest
omits unimported source from a report entirely rather than listing it at 0%, so an
unmeasured file is invisible, not visibly bad.
assert-coverage-completeness.mjs closes that by taking a census of tracked production
files and requiring each one to be either measured or named here. So this list is the
difference between a file being deliberately out of scope and a file nobody noticed.
That is why the reasons are in the repository and not in a review comment: the claim
is auditable, and it is re-tested on every run.
KINDS, AND WHAT MAKES AN ENTRY STALE
The kind is not a label; it selects which staleness test runs. An entry that stops
being true fails the gate instead of being carried forward.
harness-config -- the file configures the test runner itself. Its package does have
a harness, but the harness cannot measure its own config: jest loads
jest.config.js in the parent process before any instrumentation exists, and
collectCoverageFrom does not match it. Stale once the file stops being tracked,
or once it does appear in the coverage report.
no-harness -- no JS/TS test harness exists anywhere in this file's directory tree,
so nothing could measure it. This is a different disposition from 'measured and
uncovered', and it must not be reported as a coverage gap. Stale once the file
stops being tracked, once a package.json / tsconfig / jest or vitest config
appears in any ancestor directory, or once it turns up in a coverage report.
Both kinds are also reported when the census would not have asked about the file at
all -- a path that is not tracked production source needs no exclusion, and an entry
that guards nothing is a stale entry.
WHAT DOES NOT BELONG HERE
A file that a harness could measure but no test exercises. That is a coverage gap and
belongs in a test, not in this list. Excluding it would restore exactly the blind spot
the gate exists to remove.
Paths are repository-relative and POSIX-separated. The census covers .ts, .tsx, .mts,
.cts, .js and .mjs, minus .d.ts declarations and test sources.

exclusions.reason: jest's own config -- loaded before instrumentation exists, and collectCoverageFrom ['lib/**/*.ts','bin/**/*.ts'] cannot match a file at the package root.
jest's own config -- loaded before instrumentation exists, and collectCoverageFrom ['src/**/*.ts'] cannot match a file at the package root.

A node helper shelled out to by the Python transpiler's tools/refresh_schemas.py; its tree is a Python package (pyproject.toml, uv.lock) with no package.json, tsconfig, jest or vitest config, so no JS harness exists to measure it.

This census script itself. Invoked as `node .github/scripts/...` from a workflow step, and neither .github/scripts/, .github/ nor the repository root carries a package.json, tsconfig, jest or vitest config -- verified against `git ls-files` -- so no JS harness exists anywhere in its tree to measure it. Named here rather than left unlisted because the gate is deliberately self-inclusive: it censuses every tracked JS/TS file, including its own, and an unexplained absence is what it exists to reject.

The denominator-pinning script, same disposition as assert-coverage-completeness.mjs above: run by `node` from a workflow step, in a tree with no JS harness in any ancestor directory. These two are the only tracked JS/TS files under .github/, so this pair completes that subtree rather than starting a list that will grow with each workflow helper.
